arxiv-1710-05193.title: K-means clustering for efficient and robust registration of multi-view point sets Journal: Pattern Recognition
arxiv-1710-05193.creator: Zutao Jiang, Jihua Zhu, Georgios D. Evangelidis, Changqing Zhang, Shanmin Pang, Yaochen Li
arxiv-1710-05193.description: Abstract Generally, there are three main factors that determine the practical usability of registration, i.e., accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. In real-time applications, efficiency and robustness are more important. To promote these two abilities, we cast the multi-view registration into a clustering task.

arxiv-2206-02742.title: Understanding Self-Directed Learning in an Online Laboratory
arxiv-2206-02742.creator: Sungeun An, Spencer Rugaber Jennifer Hammock, Ashok K. Goel
arxiv-2206-02742.description: Abstract Many studies on using online laboratories for learning focus on pedagogical contexts in K-12 education with well-defined problems as well as well-defined learning goals, assessments, and outcomes. We describe a study on the use of an online laboratory for self-directed learning through the construction and simulation of conceptual models of ecological systems.

arxiv-2210-05948.title: Non-Hermitian acoustic waveguides with periodic electroacoustic feedback
arxiv-2210-05948.creator: Danilo Braghini, Vinicius D. de Lima, Danilo Beli, Matheus I. N. Rosa, José R. de F. Arruda
arxiv-2210-05948.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Danilo Braghini, Vinicius D. de Lima, Danilo Beli, Matheus I. N. Rosa, José R. de F. Arruda. In this work, we investigate non-Hermitian acoustic waveguides designed with periodically applied feedback efforts using electrodynamic actuators. One-dimensional spectral (infinite-dimensional) and finite element (finite-dimensional) models for plane acoustic waves in ducts are used. It is shown that dispersion diagrams of this family of metamaterials exhibit non-reciprocal imaginary frequency components, manifesting as wave attenuation or amplification along opposite directions for all pass bands.

arxiv-2410-04466.title: Large Language Model Inference Acceleration: A Comprehensive Hardware Perspective Thanks: SII: Shanghai Innovation Institute
arxiv-2410-04466.creator: Jinhao Li, Jiaming Xu, Shan Huang, Yonghua Chen, Wen Li, Jun Liu, Yaoxiu Lian, Jiayi Pan, Li Ding, Hao Zhou, Yu Wang, Guohao Dai
arxiv-2410-04466.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across various fields, from natural language understanding to text generation. Compared to non-generative LLMs like BERT and DeBERTa, generative LLMs like GPT series and Llama series are currently the main focus due to their superior algorithmic performance. The advancements in generative LLMs are closely intertwined with the development of hardware capabilities.

arxiv-2412-17998.title: WavePulse: Real-time Content Analytics of Radio Livestreams
arxiv-2412-17998.creator: Govind Mittal, Sarthak Gupta, Shruti Wagle, Chirag Chopra, Anthony J DeMattee, Nasir Memon, Mustaque Ahamad, Chinmay Hegde
arxiv-2412-17998.description: Abstract . Radio remains a pervasive medium for mass information dissemination, with AM/FM stations reaching more Americans than either smartphone-based social networking or live television. Increasingly, radio broadcasts are also streamed online and accessed over the Internet. We present WavePulse , a framework that records, documents, and analyzes radio content in real-time.

arxiv-2505-00511.title: Inconsistency-based Active Learning for LiDAR Object Detection
arxiv-2505-00511.creator: Esteban Rivera, Loic Stratil, Markus Lienkamp
arxiv-2505-00511.description: Abstract Deep learning models for object detection in autonomous driving have recently achieved impressive performance gains and are already being deployed in vehicles worldwide. However, current models require increasingly large datasets for training. Acquiring and labeling such data is costly, necessitating the development of new strategies to optimize this process.

arxiv-2601-02239.title: A General Class of Functionals for Certifying Quantum Incompatibility
arxiv-2601-02239.creator: Kuan-Yi Lee, Jhen-Dong Lin, Adam Miranowicz, Yueh-Nan Chen
arxiv-2601-02239.description: Abstract Quantum steering, measurement incompatibility, and instrument incompatibility have recently been recognized as unified manifestations of quantum incompatibility. Building on this perspective, we develop a general framework for constructing optimization-free, nonlinear incompatibility witnesses based on convex functionals, valid in arbitrary dimensions. munro-palaeolithic-man-1908.creator: Robert Munro
munro-palaeolithic-man-1908.description: Munro's 1908 synthesis of palaeolithic man and the lake-dwellings — the bridge between deep antiquity and European prehistory.

pmc-10647431.title: A Simple Entry to the 5,8-Disubstituted Indolizidine Skeleton via Hetero Diels-Alder Reaction
pmc-10647431.creator: Juan Francisco Rodríguez-Caro, María M Afonso, José Antonio Palenzuela, Paolo Quadrelli
pmc-10647431.description: The 5,8-disubstituted indolizidines are the largest family of indolizidines isolated from the skin of amphibians. These compounds exhibit interesting biological activities such as noncompetitive blockers of nicotinic receptors. In this paper, we present a short, simple, and general synthesis of these alkaloids based on the hetero Diels–Alder reaction between suitable monoactivated dienes and Δ1-pyrroline as the dienophile.

pmc-11351218.title: Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Leukaemia
pmc-11351218.creator: Ilayda Eroz, Prabneet Kaur Kakkar, Renal Antoinette Lazar, Jehan El-Jawhari, Biancamaria Longoni
pmc-11351218.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are one of the main residents in the bone marrow (BM) and have an essential role in the regulation of haematopoietic stem cell (HSC) differentiation and proliferation. Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDSs) are a group of myeloid disorders impacting haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSCPs) that are characterised by BM failure, ineffective haematopoiesis, cytopenia, and a high risk of transformation through the expansion of MDS clones together with additional genetic defects.

pmc-11433383.title: Experimental and Modeling Analysis of Polypropylene Fiber Reinforced Concrete Subjected to Alkali Attack and Freeze–Thaw Cycling Effect
pmc-11433383.creator: Yuxiang Huang, Yongcheng Ji, Jingchen Wang, Zihao Wang, Bosong Yu, Siyu Zhang, Eddie Koenders
pmc-11433383.description: The durability of concrete materials in harsh environmental conditions, particularly in cold regions, has garnered significant attention in civil engineering research in recent years. Concrete structures in these areas are often damaged by the combined effects of alkali–silica reaction (ASR) and freeze–thaw cycles, leading to structural cracks and significant safety hazards.

pmc-11494775.title: Oncolytic avian reovirus-sensitized tumor infiltrating CD8+ T cells triggering immunogenic apoptosis in gastric cancer
pmc-11494775.creator: Yi-Ying Wu, Feng-Hsu Wu, I-Chun Chen, Tsai-Ling Liao, Muhammad Munir, Hung-Jen Liu
pmc-11494775.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundGastric cancer (GC) is a leading malignant disease in numerous countries, including Taiwan with limited therapeutic options. Animal viruses including oncolytic avian reovirus (ARV) have the possibility to avoid pre-existing immunity in humans, while being safe and immunostimulatory.

pmc-12612505.title: Integrated analysis of the safety of fecal microbiota, live-jslm in adults with recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection from five prospective clinical trials: an update
pmc-12612505.creator: Christine Lee, Paul Feuerstadt, Thomas Louie, Lindy Bancke, Beth Guthmueller, Adam Harvey, Frederikke Hoeyer, Robert Orenstein, Erik R Dubberke, Sahil Khanna
pmc-12612505.description: Background:Fecal microbiota, live-jslm (RBL) is approved in the United States and Canada for prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI) in adults following standard-of-care (SOC) antibiotic treatment.Objectives:Provide an updated integrated safety analysis, incorporating final safety data from Punch CD3-OLS.Design:Safety data were combined from five RBL trials: three phase II and two phase III trials.

pmc-12714287.title: Co-isolation of genetically distinct Burkholderia pseudomallei strains from a single patient in North Queensland
pmc-12714287.creator: Pauline M. L. Coulon, Piklu Roy Chowdhury, Ian Gassiep, Kay Ramsay, Aven Lee, Edita Ritmejeryte, Miranda E. Pitt, Joyce To, Sarah Reed, Patrick N. A. Harris, Garry S. A. Myers, William C. Nierman, William C. Nierman, William C. Nierman
pmc-12714287.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). While investigating colony morphology variation within clinical isolates of Burkholderia pseudomallei (Bp) isolated from a single clinical infection, we identified two distinct strains (based on their multi-locus sequence type) from Bp TSV292. Reports of simultaneous co-infection are un-common, with only two studies in Thailand documenting such cases: (1) 2 out of 133 cases, and (2) 13 out of 59 patients infected with two to three polyclonal Bp strains exhibiting different genotypes.

pmc-12830929.title: Fragmented QRS duration as a marker of cardiac and hepatic iron overload: across-sectional study
pmc-12830929.creator: Seyyed Bozorgmehr Hedayati, Soodeh Hooshmandi, Raheb Ghorbani, Mohammad Kamali, Mohammad Hashem Arabkhani
pmc-12830929.description: Thalassemia is a group of hematological disorders brought about by defective globin chains synthesis, which can indirectly culminate in hepatic and myocardial cellular damages through iron deposition. The purpose of this study is to examine the relationship between fragmented QRS duration and liver T2* value.

pmc-12965689.title: Exploring the importance and preference of sugar feeding behaviour of malaria vectors in sugar plantations of southern Malawi
pmc-12965689.creator: Kennedy Zembere, Sylvester Coleman, James Chirombo, Rex Mbewe, Julie-Anne Tangena
pmc-12965689.description: BackgroundReliable tools are needed to control opportunistic outdoor biting and resting malaria vectors that remain beyond the reach of indoor targeted interventions. The attractive targeted sugar baits (ATSBs) have demonstrated effectiveness in some settings but have shown limited impact in other areas, in part due to differences in mosquito species’ preferences and the presence of competing natural sugar sources.

pmc-13111478.title: NO- and S-nitrosothiols-dependent relaxation in large and small resistance blood vessels
pmc-13111478.creator: Mauricio A. Lillo, Annie Beuve
pmc-13111478.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Nitric oxide (NO) has long been viewed as the principal endothelium-derived vasodilator through activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase (GC1) and cGMP-dependent signaling in vascular smooth muscle. However, accumulating evidence indicates that this canonical NO-GC1-cGMP pathway predominates in large conduit arteries, whereas regulation of vascular tone and blood pressure in the microcirculation relies largely on endothelium-derived hyperpolarization (EDH) with NO acting primarily as a redox signal rather than a freely diffusing gas.

pmc-13333533.title: Early‐Onset Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Emerging Biological Insights, Risk Factors and Clinical Implications
pmc-13333533.creator: Gennaro Musella, Cristina D'Antonio, Federica Canfora, Michele D Mignogna, Valentino Vellone, Vito Carlo Alberto Caponio, Amerigo Giudice, Alessandro Villa, Daniela Adamo
pmc-13333533.description: BackgroundEarly‐onset oral squamous cell carcinoma (EO‐OSCC), commonly defined as occurring in individuals under 50 years of age, is increasingly recognized as a potentially distinct clinical subset with differences in exposure patterns and tumor biology compared with conventional oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC).

pmc-13390105.title: Observations about left atrial tachycardias: Broadening our understanding
pmc-13390105.creator: Steven M. Markowitz
pmc-13390105.description: . Such cases of so-called de novo atypical flutter present challenges for the clinician. For example, should an ablation procedure target only the presenting arrhythmia, or are more extensive lesion sets required to achieve optimal long-term outcomes? What is the appropriate endpoint for ablation of atypical flutters?

pmc-13648136.title: Basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma of the hands in an orthopedic surgeon with occupational radiation exposure from C-arm fluoroscopy in Korea: a case report
pmc-13648136.creator: Jisue Yoon, Jihye Lee, Seongjin Jeong, Sangchul Roh, Min-Gi Kim, Jeongbae Rhie
pmc-13648136.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundOccupational radiation exposure among medical professionals who use fluoroscopic devices is a well-recognized concern. While radiation-induced skin cancer has been reported in interventional radiologists, cases involving orthopedic surgeons with prolonged C-arm fluoroscopy exposure have rarely been described.

pmc-13672137.title: Low‐Complexity Phase–Transition‐Based VO2 Transmissive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Indoor Millimeter‐Wave Communications
pmc-13672137.creator: Junghyeon Kim, Sumin Bark, Minjae Lee, Sungjoon Lim
pmc-13672137.description: This paper presents a low‐complexity and low‐cost transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (TRIS) based on the phase‐change material vanadium dioxide (VO2) for indoor millimeter‐wave (mm‐wave) communications. Although mm‐wave systems enable ultra‐high data rates and low latency, their performance is limited by severe path loss and non‐line‐of‐sight propagation. RISs offer a promising solution by dynamically controlling electromagnetic wave propagation.

pmc-13677444.title: Evaluating HEART: Student Engagement and Health System Impact in a Person‐Centered Learning Health System Initiative
pmc-13677444.creator: Tracey Carr, Stefanie Foster, Phoebe Stobart, Carson Squair, Taylor Spock, Candace Skrapek, Margaret King, Brenda Andreas, Noelle Rohatinsky, Christine Stobart, Caitlin Ward, Tina Zheng, Gerald Farthing
pmc-13677444.description: BackgroundHealthcare Education and Research Training (HEART) is a cocurricular, engaged learning initiative that supported undergraduate students in acquiring and applying healthcare research skills. The project was guided by a learning health system (LHS)‐aligned model focused on the collection, synthesis, and rapid translation of patient‐reported experience data into actionable recommendations.
